Subject: Renewal sync — retainer & scale playbook (usage variance + recommendations)

Hi Lily,

Thanks again for the time last week. I pulled together a short usage recap for Q1 and a recommended retainer/scale playbook to keep PixelHealth on predictable costs as you move into heavier inference for triage and discharge summaries. Key highlights in the attached report:

- Token spend: month-to-month variance of 28% (avg 3.7M tokens/day in Feb -> 4.7M in Mar) driven by increased nightly batch jobs.
- Latency: p95 increased from 210ms to 310ms during 00:00–03:00 UTC spikes (see latency_dashboard_202704.png).
- ROI signal: model latency improvement after smaller batch tuning reduced token cost per successful inference by ~9% on our test set.

Recommendations (high level):
1) Move to a small dedicated pool with burst credit to handle nightly batch surge (reduces fallback to hosted variants).
2) Add a prefix-KV cache for templated discharge summaries (estimate 12–18% token saving).
3) Shift 15% of lower-criticality generation to quantized model variant for cost reduction while keeping 95th percentile latency SLOs for real-time flows.

I can walk through the report on a 30-min sync — are you available Wed or Thu? If helpful I’ll include Marissa (platform economics) and Ben (ops) to map the rollout timeline.

Best,
Jordan

Jordan — thanks for the summary and attachments, looks helpful. Quick answers:

- Yes, the nightly batch was increased March 4 when we enabled the outbound summaries for the pilot cohort. We expected the step-up but not the latency degradation.
- We need to keep realtime workflows (ER triage) at <300ms p95; anything above starts to affect clinician adoption.
- Budget: procurement has a rough ceiling for the retainer; we can increase committed spend if we see clear unit-cost savings.

Wed 10am PT works for me; procurement will be on the call to discuss contract shape. Please include the proposed ratecard.

Lily

Perfect — booked Wed 2027-04-28 10:00 PT. Attaching a draft ratecard and a 2-slide ops playbook so procurement has visibility (attached: proposed_ratecard_PH_v2.xlsx).

Quick clarifications for the call so we can keep it to 30 minutes:
- Target retainer bands: S (3 GPUs reserved) / M (6 GPUs) / L (12 GPUs) with burst credits; I’ll highlight expected effective token unit price for each.
- Measured savings assumptions: 12% from prefix caching, 9% from quantization for non-real-time flows, and additional 6–8% from smarter request routing when load is high.
- Fallback policy: automatic fallback to lower-tier model when dedicated pool saturated — we can set per-route guardrails for ER triage so it never drops below p95 300ms.

Marissa/Ben — would you two mind preparing (1) an ops rollout checklist (Ben) and (2) a short cost-model slide that shows effective $/k tokens across the three retainer bands (Marissa)? We’ll use those on Wed.

Thanks — looking forward.

Jordan

Hi all — I ran the effective unit economics using PixelHealth's Q1 profile (attached: usage_report_Q1-2027.pdf and a short rate rundown). Toplines:

- If PixelHealth moves to the M retainer (6 GPUs with burst credits + prefix caching), our model shows an expected annualized token spend reduction of ~22% versus current on-demand mix, netting effective $/M tokens 18% lower than current effective rate.
- Break-even vs current spend: ~5 months assuming retention of current traction and no additional product features that materially change token distribution.
- Risk note: if nightly batch growth continues >35% month-over-month we should re-evaluate burst sizing quickly; ops can add temporary burst credits within 48 hours.

Attachment: latency_dashboard_202704.png highlights p95 windows; ops suggestion is a minor tuning pass to batching params and deploying prefix-KV cache for the templates used in the nightly job — both low-risk.

I’ll present the cost slide on Wed and bring the modeling workbook to share live.

—Marissa
